newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- up 1/8 ahead of Friday data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPALS -- up 1/8 ahead of Friday data.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices gained about 1/8 point Thursday, but trading was cautious ahead of the key Friday jobs report.
"It was kind of a mixed bag today, with a slightly better tone but a few bid-wanteds," one trader said. He judged the cash market up as high as 1/4 point in spots.

Market participants said the June jobs report, set for release at 0830 EDT Friday, would set the tone in the near term. Economists surveyed by Reuters expected the report to show a 193,000 increase in non-farm payrolls and a 4.9 percent unemployment rate.

On the new issue front, Lehman Brothers said it repriced Thursday's largest deal, an $811 million bond issue from Arapahoe County, Colo.'s E-470 Public Highway Authority. Lehman said it lowered yields in several maturities.
PaineWebber Inc won the largest competitive offering, a $101 million Wisconsin general obligation issue which the firm reoffered at 5.15 percent in 2018.
PaineWebber said later in the day it had a $51 million balance left to sell.
Muni secondary traders said gains were hard to come by given lots of new supply and waning demand at the new yield levels.
U.S. Treasury prices see-sawed in early action, then gained ground in the afternoon on technical buying that included some muni defeasance action.
The government long bond rose 13/32 to 104-11/32, to yield 6.30 percent.
In the muni secondary market, bids on Fairfax County Water Authority, Va., 5.0s of 2029 were up one basis point from Wednesday, to 5.29 percent.
Jefferson County, Ala., FGIC 5-3/4s of 2027 were also one basis point higher, at 5.27 percent.

September municipal bond contracts climbed 3/32 to 122-5/32 on the day, while September Treasury bond futures gained 12/32 to 116-24/32. The MOB spread narrowed to 173 ticks from 182 at the close on Wednesday.

In economic data released Thursday, first-time jobless claims for the latest week fell to the lowest level in more than 23 years. The data showed claims slipping to 277,000 in the week ended July 26 from 299,000 in the previous week. That undershot Wall Street economists' consensus forecast for 306,000 of claims.

The Commerce Department said the second quarter Gross Domestic Product rose 2.2 percent compared to a revised 4.9 percent in the first quarter. Economists surveyed by Reuters had expected a 1.9 percent gain.
